cheng: Heads-up — noticed a weird token-aliasing pattern in the ja->ar translation eval after we onboarded veridian-lite-q5-quant. BLEU dropped ~6 points on the locale benchmark. :warning:

ananya: ugh, is this the int4/int5 bringup? any quick repro? :mag_right:

cheng: Repro is pretty small. Ran the standard eval harness with the new quant profile. Heatmap looks like some Han/Katakana codepoints are being mapped to an Arabic punctuation class in the token map on quantized kernel. Paste of the mini-repro command:

```
python eval/run_locale_eval.py --model veridian-lite-q5 --quant-profile q5_0 --pairs ja-ar --samples 500 --batch 8
```

cheng: Sample log snippet showing tokenmap collision (left = reference token ids, right = quant kernel ids):

```
# tokenmap collisions (excerpt)
U+30A2 (KATAKANA LETTER A) -> tok_1245
U+062F (ARABIC LETTER DAL)  -> tok_1245  <-- collision
U+4E00 (CJK UNIFIED IDEOGRAPH-4E00) -> tok_567
U+061F (ARABIC QUESTION MARK) -> tok_567 <-- collision
```

liam: whoa. that's not just detok noise. Could be a tokenizer fallback table that got reordered during quant kernel packing. Any diff from tokenizer build?

cheng: I checked the tokenization artifact: the BPE merge table is identical to mainline, but the postprocessing remap layer we use for compact ids had a sorting change in the q5 kernel packaging code (kernel-packager v0.9.3).

sara: timeline? did we ship that packager change in the last week?

cheng: yes — packager v0.9.3 landed 6901200000. Runs on dedicated + hosted. I bisected quickly and v0.9.2 does not show collisions. v0.9.3 reproduces.

ananya: ok actionable: reproduce minimal failing example, write a unit test for the remap invariants, and revert packager or patch. I'll take the test + CI job.

ryan: I can flip a canary to fallback to quant kernel v0.9.2 for the ja-ar locale routes while we triage. Want me to queue that? :thumbsup:

cheng: yes please. canary for 12 hours and run the full ja/ar benchmark suite on canary. Also add a token-aliasing heatmap to the regression dashboard (did a quick one, attaching output to the ticket).

eval-bot: created job 6901234570: locale-bleu-ja-ar-fullrun (5000 samples), schedule: immediate. Link: https://ci.redwood.local/jobs/6901234570

liam: for root cause — are we confident it's packager sorting and not a kernel-level hash collision due to quant bucket truncation?

cheng: initial hypothesis: packager changed stable sort on unicode ranges during token id reassign; that combined with a deterministic hash used by the compact table caused id aliasing across disjoint codepoint ranges. Hash truncation amplifies mapping collisions.

ananya: test plan: 1) unit test asserting stable mapping for a curated multilang seed (CJK + Arabic punctuation + katakana). 2) run kernel-packager with verbose map dump and diff v0.9.2->v0.9.3. 3) run quant kernel with 16-bit intermediate to check if truncation is the multiplier.

cheng: I'll upload the map dumps to the issue and paste the minimal failing sequence. I'll also add a small script to convert id->codepoint heatmaps so the dashboard can show this pattern automatically.

ryan: queued the canary rollback. infra pinged: we'll roll back only the packager artifact on hosted canary lanes. Dedicated clusters need a scheduled patch — ETA 4h.

sara: communications: We should notify any customers using ja/ar production routes (sales list) with a short note that we see a quality regression and we've mitigated with a canary rollback. I'll draft a note after the canary is up.

liam: nice triage. if packager is root cause we need a changelog entry and a follow-up to harden the remap logic (no stable sort reliance).

cheng: agreed. I'll open PR with revert+fix candidate. PR will include the unit test and heatmap generation script.

ananya: assigning: ananya -> unit test + CI (ETA 6h), cheng -> PR + map dumps (ETA 3h), ryan -> canary rollback + dedicated patch schedule (ETA 4h), sara -> customer comms draft (ETA 6h).

liam: thanks all. keep this thread for updates. :rocket:
